blocks.text:
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                ANCIENT ATHLETIC TRADITIONS                       |
|                                                                  |
|  GREEK WORLD            ROMAN WORLD          MESOAMERICA         |
|  -----------            ----------           -----------         |
|  Panhellenic Games      Ludi (public games)  Ulama / Pok-a-tok   |
|  Olympics (Olympia)     Gladiatorial combat  Rubber ball game    |
|  Pythian (Delphi)       Venatio (beast hunt) 1500+ courts        |
|  Isthmian (Corinth)     Circus Maximus       Ritual sacrifice    |
|  Nemean (Nemea)         Chariot racing       Hip/knee/thigh only |
|                                                                  |
|  Sacred to Zeus         State spectacle      Religious embedded  |
|  Civic/religious        Political tool       Victory = cosmic    |
|  4-year cycle           Annual ludi          significance        |
|  Nudity / gymnos        Amphitheater/circus  Stone ring goals    |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

Common thread: sport embedded in religious and civic ritual,
not isolated entertainment. The separation of "sport" from
"ceremony" is a modern construction.

PANKRATION COMPARISON TO MODERN MMA:
  :------------------:------------------:
  | Ancient Pankration | Modern MMA     |
  :------------------:------------------:
  | No weight classes | Weight classes  |
  | No rounds        | Timed rounds     |
  | No ring boundary | Cage/ring        |
  | No ref stoppage  | Referee stops    |
  | Bite/gouge banned| Many rules       |
  | All else legal   | Unified rules    |
  | Won: sub/KO/death| Won: sub/KO/dec  |
  :------------------:------------------:
  Conceptually identical. Ancient pankration IS
  ancient MMA. Rules simply fewer.

COLOSSEUM (Flavian Amphitheater, 80 CE)
  Capacity: ~50,000-80,000 (debated)
  Events: Gladiatorial combat, venatio, executions

  Structure:
  +------------------------------------------+
  |  Velarium (awning) -- shaded spectators  |
  |  Tiers: senatorial / equestrian /        |
  |    plebeian / women/slaves (top)         |
  |  80 arches on each of 4 floors           |
  |  Hypogeum (underground): animal pens,    |
  |    gladiator holding cells, elevators    |
  +------------------------------------------+

CIRCUS MAXIMUS (Rome)
  Capacity: ~150,000-250,000 (largest ever)
  Used primarily for chariot racing
  Primary track: ~540m long, 150m wide
  Spina (central barrier) with turning posts
  7 laps = 1 race (~5km)

  Chariot factions (factiones):
  Blue (Veneta)  Green (Prasina) -- most popular
  Red (Russata)  White (Albata)  -- less prominent

  Faction support was quasi-political:
  Emperor Caligula dined with Green faction
  Nika riots (532 CE) started as Blue-Green rivalry,
  became political revolt -- 30,000 dead

:------------------------------------------------------:
|          ANCIENT SPORT COMMON STRUCTURE              |
|                                                      |
|  ALL THREE TRADITIONS share:                         |
|                                                      |
|  1. RELIGIOUS EMBEDDING                              |
|     -- Greek: sacred to Zeus, Pythian to Apollo      |
|     -- Roman: ludi originated as funeral rites       |
|     -- Mesoamerican: ball game = cosmic ritual       |
|                                                      |
|  2. CIVIC/POLITICAL FUNCTION                         |
|     -- Greek: city-state prestige via champions      |
|     -- Roman: rulers used games for political control|
|     -- Mesoamerican: elite display/tribute system    |
|                                                      |
|  3. PROFESSIONAL ATHLETICISM                         |
|     -- Greek: full-time trained athletes, coaches    |
|     -- Roman: gladiators were specialized, trained   |
|     -- Mesoamerican: court players were specialists  |
|                                                      |
|  4. SPECTATOR CULTURE                                |
|     -- Greek: 45,000 at Olympia stadium              |
|     -- Roman: 250,000 Circus Maximus                 |
|     -- Mesoamerican: elevated viewing areas          |
|                                                      |
|  5. MORTALITY RISK NORMALIZED                        |
|     -- Greek pankration: deaths occurred             |
|     -- Roman munera: ~20% death rate per bout        |
|     -- Mesoamerican: ritual sacrifice linked         |
+------------------------------------------------------+
